output.summary: Deterministic verdict: FAIL (window policy summary verdict FAIL; business_verdict FAIL; resource_verdict NO_POLICY; run_validity VALID). The overall-errors policy check fails: observed error rate 3688/73813 (~5.0%) exceeds the 0.01 (1%) threshold in the run-intersection window. All 3688 JMeter sampler errors belong to the checkout transaction (the other five transaction summaries report 0 errors); OpenSearch groups them as frontend.request_error at service frontend (count 3688, error_rate_per_minute 258.8) with intermittent bursts up to 1244 errors/minute. Checkout also shows an extreme max latency of 10008 ms versus 980-1071 ms for the other transactions. Resource coverage is INCOMPLETE: paymentservice CPU/memory have RESOURCE_GAPS (5 and 6 missing cells of 47). The errors-vs-load correlation is descriptive only (raw rho 0.9744, partial rho 0.9722 at best_lag_ms 0; uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED; headline selection UNAVAILABLE/GENUINE_PARTIAL_UNCALIBRATED), and clock_alignment is not_verified_by_core, so no causal or lead/lag claim is supported by the analysis. Advice does not change the FAIL verdict.

caveats: Analysis coverage is INCOMPLETE: paymentservice CPU and memory summaries have RESOURCE_GAPS (5 and 6 missing cells of 47, longest_gap_cells 2), so resource-side conclusions about paymentservice are not supported.
Correlation uncertainty is NOT_ESTIMATED and the headline selection is UNAVAILABLE with reason GENUINE_PARTIAL_UNCALIBRATED; rho values are descriptive only and do not prove that load caused errors.

clock_alignment is not_verified_by_core, with dropped_leading_cells 1 and dropped_trailing_cells 1 within the run-intersection window; temporal lead/lag or causal hypotheses require clock verification first.
resource_verdict is NO_POLICY; a missing resource policy is not a pass and is not evidence that resource usage or capacity was healthy.
The diagnostic summary reports anomalies_tested 0 and episodes_reported 0 (status COMPLETE, uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED); this does not demonstrate stability or absence of problems.

The overall metric summary uses sample_count 75411 (error rate 3688/75411 ~4.9%) while the window policy check uses denominator 73813 (~5.0%) because of run-intersection trimming; both exceed the 1% threshold.

All sampler errors are attributed to the checkout transaction, while OpenSearch records them as frontend.request_error at service frontend; the mapping between the JMeter sampler and the OpenSearch error group is not explicitly demonstrated.

The checkout max latency of 10008 ms is extreme compared with other transactions (<=1071 ms), but the temporal relationship of those samples to the 3688 errors is not established by the summarized evidence.
Error log messages are generic ('request error') with no response codes, stack traces, or downstream service details in the evidence, so the root cause of checkout errors is unresolved.

The OpenSearch error timeline spans a wider snapshot (1790628720000 to 1790629575000 ms) than the evaluation window (1790628795000 to 1790629500000 ms); correlation pairing used 47 cells within the evaluation window.
The run is VALID and the verdict FAIL is deterministic; the hypotheses and recommendations in this advice do not alter that verdict.
